PullRequest.Title: sessions: Fix unified remote host picker behavior
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary
- keep the unified workspace picker and its Remote submenu open while configured host rows are removed
- preserve and refresh live nested action-list submenus, including their filter and focus state
- show remote harness names without repeating the host already selected in the workspace picker
- let workspace-less Chat target Local or any eligible remote Agent Host
- add real toolbar-interaction, picker-routing, and remote quick-chat regression coverage

## Validation
- `npm run compile-client`
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/actionWidget/test/browser/actionList.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/sessionWorkspacePicker.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/newChatWidget.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/browser/remoteAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts`
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/browser/remoteAgentHost.contribution.test.ts`

Fixes #336552
Fixes #336538
Fixes #336544

Scenarios.Scenario: A visible unified workspace picker refreshes after provider registration/removal, session-type changes, configuration/file changes, or Dev Container availability changes.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The event synchronously rebuilds picker item descriptors and updates the existing ActionList DOM; only row-count changes request outer context-view layout. Dev Container availability checks are queued asynchronously and are off the immediate refresh critical path, with a later 50 ms coalesced refresh after the limiter drains.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check each eligible recent workspace for .devcontainer configuration through hasDevContainerConfiguration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one check per unique provider/workspace cache key after an invalidation; warm builds reuse the boolean or in-flight promise. Effective parallelism is capped at 4.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same cache invalidation and _buildItems path ran through showPicker, so the same cold checks occurred before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Queued asynchronously; the first build renders without the Dev Container mode action and a coalesced follow-up refresh incorporates results.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query Dev Container service Docker availability after a workspace has matching configuration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to one IPC query for each effective cold workspace key whose filesystem check succeeds, under the same global Limiter(4).
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Full picker reconstruction invoked the same availability path and cardinality before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous and off the initial UI refresh critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of registered providers, deduplicated recent workspaces, menu actions, and remote submenu rows. Item construction and list replacement are linear in those bounded collections; Dev Container checks use unique provider/workspace keys.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Provider/session events are handled serially on the UI event loop. Dev Container availability work is shared through a per-picker key cache and a Limiter(4); the refresh scheduler coalesces drain-triggered refreshes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm provider/workspace keys avoid new availability boundaries; in-flight promises also coalesce duplicate builds. Provider/configuration/file/availability changes deliberately clear the cache, and the limiter drain schedules one delayed refresh.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the event handlers, cache key, limiter, scheduler, item builder, and ActionList update/layout calls are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Recent-workspace and provider counts vary, but the diff replaces full popup teardown/recreation with in-place list refresh for the unified picker and does not increase boundary cardinality.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The changed unified path preserves the submenu while doing no more boundary work than the previous full rebuild and generally reduces DOM reconstruction.

Scenarios.Scenario: A user removes a configured remote host from the open Remote submenu.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The toolbar action invokes removeRemoteHost; provider removal then rebuilds parent items and updates the open nested ActionList. Focus/filter state and the submenu are retained instead of tearing down the whole picker.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Disconnect/remove the selected remote host through the provider or remote agent host service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One selected host per user action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same onRemove action and one-host boundary existed; the picker previously closed/reopened rather than refreshing its live submenu.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The remove action awaits completion; provider-change UI refresh follows the resulting state change.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist removal of a configured WebSocket host through configuration storage when the provider lacks its own remove/disconnect method.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One configuration update per selected host removal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited by the explicit remove action.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of rows in the open remote submenu; one parent and one child list are rebuilt linearly after a removal.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One removal per activated toolbar action. Pointer propagation suppression prevents the same click from also selecting the row; no new fan-out or background burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The provider change clears Dev Container availability state; any later checks are re-keyed and bounded as in the picker-refresh scenario. No removal cache is involved.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: event propagation, remove callback, provider event, nested update, and layout flow are directly visible.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A submenu can contain many recents/providers, but removal is user-paced and the prior implementation reconstructed the entire picker.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The new work is bounded, user-triggered, and replaces a more disruptive full widget reconstruction.

Scenarios.Scenario: A desktop user opens the workspace picker and starts a workspace-less Chat on Local or a selected remote Agent Host.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opening the picker synchronously enumerates registered providers and allocates one action per eligible ungrouped quick-chat provider. Selecting one action creates exactly one provider-owned draft; a connected Agent Host may eagerly start one backend session after authentication.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start the chosen Agent Host backend session when the selected provider is connected and authentication has settled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One backend session for the single explicitly selected provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Remote Agent Host providers were not advertised as quick-chat targets, so this explicit remote-host quick-chat path was unavailable; default/local quick chat already created one provider draft.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Triggered only after the user selects Local or a remote host; draft construction/activation is on the selection path while backend startup proceeds through the provider lifecycle.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of eligible providers controls only the small in-memory submenu and action allocations; execution cardinality remains one selected provider.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Provider enumeration is synchronous with no boundary calls. Selection targets one provider and starts one draft/backend path; there is no Promise.all or per-provider connection burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache or retry loop is added for provider enumeration. Existing provider/session state determines whether backend startup can proceed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: provider filtering, action callback, management resolution, draft creation, and eager backend start are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider counts and remote connection latency vary, but the operation is explicitly requested and does not fan out across hosts.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The one remote boundary is the intended behavior of the new selectable target and is not duplicated or moved onto picker opening.

Scenarios.Scenario: Action widgets handle pointer interaction, focus transitions, and live submenu replacement.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each widget mousedown performs a timestamp write. A blur schedules one replaceable 75 ms timeout and may defer dismissal until at most one second after the last internal mousedown. Live submenu updates replace visible rows and perform bounded synchronous layout reads/writes.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: DOM work scales linearly with visible parent/submenu rows per explicit update; pointer bookkeeping is constant per event.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: MutableDisposable ensures at most one pending blur-hide timeout per widget; focus clears it. DOM handlers are disposed with rendered rows/widgets.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved. Timers and listeners are tied to DisposableStore/MutableDisposable lifecycles and are cleared on focus or widget disposal.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: timer ownership, listener disposal, List.splice, and submenu layout callbacks are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact layout cost varies by row count and browser, but refresh events are not frame-frequency input and prior behavior rebuilt and laid out the full widget.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. There is no accumulating timer/listener retention, and in-place updates do not add a hotter or more scalable layout path than the previous reconstruction.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 12 changed files and relevant call paths. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression was found; changed refresh work is bounded and generally replaces full widget reconstruction, while new remote quick chat performs one user-selected provider operation without fan-out.
